record.paper_title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions
record.original_question: Can a classical de Sitter solution of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources, in the standard smeared compactification ansatz on a compact 6-dimensional group manifold with constant fluxes, simultaneously have large internal volume, weak string coupling, a bounded number of orientifold planes, and quantized fluxes, or is that combination impossible?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we stick to the common ansatz of smeared solutions on group manifolds with constant fluxes; (dis)proving the following conjectures for it is a well-defined question.
Conjecture 3 Classical de Sitter solutions cannot have at the same time a large internal volume, a small string coupling, a bounded number of orientifolds and quantized fluxes.
This conjecture has been recently motivated and studied in [40–42] that considered particular cases or (many) concrete examples, without obtaining a general proof.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider ten-dimensional type II supergravity (type IIA or type IIB) compactified on a compact six-dimensional group manifold M_6 (a quotient of a six-dimensional Lie group by a discrete subgroup), with the following standard "smeared" ansatz:

(i) The ten-dimensional spacetime is a warped product dS_4 × M_6 of four-dimensional de Sitter space and M_6, in the regime where warping is dropped and the metric on M_6 is left-invariant.

(ii) The bosonic content includes the dilaton φ (assumed constant on M_6), the NSNS three-form H, and the RR field strengths F_q. All form fluxes are taken to be left-invariant (constant) on M_6.

(iii) Sources are present in the form of Op-planes and/or Dp-branes (for some fixed p ∈ {3,4,5,6,7,8}) wrapping calibrated cycles, smeared over their transverse directions, with their localized contributions to the Bianchi identities replaced by their integrated charges.

For such a solution, define:
 • The internal volume V = vol(M_6) measured in string units ℓ_s = √α′.
 • The string coupling g_s = e^{φ}.
 • The orientifold number N_O = total number of Op-planes appearing in the source content (counted with multiplicity in the relevant homology class).
 • Quantized fluxes: the periods of H/(2π α′) and of the F_q/(2π α′)^{(q)} over integral cycles of M_6 are required to take integer values.

Question: Does there exist any classical de Sitter solution of the above kind that simultaneously satisfies all four of the following conditions?

 (a) Large internal volume: V can be made arbitrarily large (V → ∞);
 (b) Weak string coupling: g_s can be made arbitrarily small (g_s → 0);
 (c) Bounded orientifold number: N_O remains bounded by a fixed constant independent of the limits in (a), (b);
 (d) Properly quantized fluxes as defined above.

Equivalently: prove or disprove that no solution in this class can realize (a)–(d) simultaneously.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains an open problem. Searches turn up only partial results and concrete case studies (e.g. work on parametric control of classical de Sitter solutions in 2024 and "Almost classical de Sitter?" JHEP 2024), with no general proof or counterexample. Recent papers explicitly describe the conjecture as motivated and tested in particular cases without a general proof.

status_evidence.title: On classical de Sitter solutions and parametric control (JHEP 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: analytic scaling has been found that makes four out of six compactification radii and the overall volume arbitrarily large, ... potentially constituting counterexamples to conjectures stating that asymptotic de Sitter solutions do not exist
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024 the conjecture is still being tested; possible counterexamples or refinements are under active investigation, no general proof exists.

status_evidence.title: Almost classical de Sitter? (JHEP 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: The classical-de Sitter scenario ... proposes to search for de Sitter vacua of orientifold flux compactifications in a regime where string corrections ... are negligible.
status_evidence.claim: The status of classical de Sitter solutions in the controlled regime remains an open question being actively examined.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions (arXiv:1902.10093)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical de Sitter solutions cannot have at the same time a large internal volume, a small string coupling, a bounded number of orientifolds and quantized fluxes.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem with only partial evidence from concrete cases.
